headline: T1 upgrade/accounting powers exist behind a verified 10-day timelock owner, but proposer/executor, multisig signers and governance distribution were not reconstructed.

findings.text: LP/eETH/Admin/Oracle/WRNFT owner() read as timelock 0x9f26d4C958fD811A1F59B01B86Be7dFFc9d20761.
Core is UUPS/proxied; LP/Admin upgrades route to RoleRegistry.onlyProtocolUpgrader; RoleRegistry source restricts that to owner().
Timelock getMinDelay() = 864000 seconds and exposes schedule/execute.
Reachable Safe/multisig owners and thresholds were not fetched.
No Governor constants were identified or read.
Pause/unpause uses RoleRegistry PROTOCOL_PAUSER/UNPAUSER; no max duration found.
Worst tier T1: upgrade/accounting/rebase/mint-burn/withdrawal-finalization surfaces can affect user funds or exits.

steelman.red: If the timelock or RoleRegistry owner path is an EOA or 2-of-3, T1 powers sit behind a weak actor.
steelman.orange: T1 powers and a 10-day delay are verified, but actual controlling actors are incomplete.
steelman.green: Green would require proving broad governance or a qualifying Security Council controls the timelock path.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because T1 powers and the 864000 second delay are verified, but the actor set controlling timelock/RoleRegistry was not proven green-grade.

evidence.shows: LP owner timelock; proxy; RoleRegistry; upgrade/pause/rebase writes.
LP source: UUPS, pauser roles, upgrade via RoleRegistry.
Admin owner timelock; oracle/LP; rebase APR/wait fields.
Admin source: executeTasks; pause roles; upgrade via RoleRegistry.
RoleRegistry verified ABI: pauser roles, owner, roleHolders, onlyProtocolUpgrader.
RoleRegistry source: owner-controlled roles; onlyProtocolUpgrader only owner().

unknowns: C2: weETH/RedemptionManager implementation resolution incomplete.
C3: Timelock role holders not read.
C4: Safe owners/thresholds not fetched.
C5: Governor/quorum/voting period not found.
C6: Pauser/unpauser holders not read.

protocol_metadata.about: Users stake ETH for eETH/weETH receipts; exits route through WithdrawRequestNFT/PriorityWithdrawalQueue; oracle/admin reports update rewards, fees and withdrawals.

headline: Standard exits are on-chain, but finalized-withdrawal claims are whenNotPaused and no maximum pause duration was found.

findings.text: Exit functions: LP requestWithdraw/requestWithdrawWithPermit/requestMembershipNFTWithdraw/withdraw; WRNFT requestWithdraw/claimWithdraw/batchClaimWithdraw; PriorityQueue request/cancel/claim/batchClaim/fulfill.
LP, WRNFT and PriorityQueue exit/claim paths are whenNotPaused; PriorityQueue request placement is onlyWhitelisted.
Pause uses PROTOCOL_PAUSER and unpause uses PROTOCOL_UNPAUSER; no cap found.
No separate time-capped emergency pause was proven.
WRNFT nextRequestId 78886, lastFinalizedRequestId 78875; no standard max queue duration found. PriorityQueue MIN_DELAY 3600, active requests 0.
No forced exit usable while claims are paused was identified.
Exit methods are on-chain and directly callable when unpaused.

steelman.red: Finalized withdrawal claims are pause-gated with no fetched cap.
steelman.orange: Withdraw/request/claim functions exist on-chain and were unpaused.
steelman.green: Green would require claims pause-exempt or short auto-expiring pause.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because finalized-withdrawal claim functions are pause-gated, no pause cap was found, and pauser holders were not proven constrained.

evidence.shows: WRNFT paused false; lastFinalized 78875; nextRequestId 78886; claim/finalize/invalidate/pause writes.
WRNFT source: claimWithdraw/batchClaim whenNotPaused; pause roles.
PriorityQueue MIN_DELAY 3600; paused false; active requests 0.
PriorityQueue source: request onlyWhitelisted/whenNotPaused; claim/cancel whenNotPaused.

unknowns: E3: Current pauser/unpauser/admin/request-manager holders not read.
E4: Pause governance/emergency distinction not reconstructed.
E5: Standard queue max duration not found.
E6: No pause-resistant escape hatch found.
E7: UX beyond direct calls not exhaustively enumerated.

protocol_metadata.about: Users stake ETH for eETH/weETH receipts; exits route through WithdrawRequestNFT/PriorityWithdrawalQueue; oracle/admin reports update rewards, fees and withdrawals.

headline: A 2-of-3 oracle report path can affect withdrawal invalidation/finalization; current locked-withdrawal exposure is about 1.25% of verified pooled ETH, while accounting performance touches about 100%.

findings.text: LP depends on Admin, WRNFT, PriorityQueue, eETH and RoleRegistry; Admin depends on Oracle, LP, WRNFT and managers.
Oracle has 3 members and quorum 2; Admin executeTasks consumes oracle consensus and processes rewards, fees, validators and withdrawals.
Docs/repo show cross-chain weETH/ETHFI and LayerZero support; material bridge TVL/trust model not quantified.
ETH to eETH/weETH staking/restaking receipt exposure; node-operator diversification/bonding not verified.
Mitigations found: 2-of-3 consensus, 50-slot wait, 500 bps rebase APR bound, 20% fee cap; no withdrawal-invalidation fallback found.
No ether.fi-operated appchain/sequencer dependency found.
Reports/execution/finalization need off-chain reporting and role-held execution; liveness failure can stall rewards/withdrawals.
Admin/governance can mutate oracle/manager dependencies, but exit window not reconstructed.

steelman.red: A 2-of-3 oracle report plus authorized execution can invalidate/finalize withdrawals, affecting queued principal.
steelman.orange: Reward APR and fees are bounded and locked withdrawals were about 1.25% of pooled ETH.
steelman.green: Green would require reports unable to harm principal or a live challenge/fallback path.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because oracle/reporting can affect withdrawal invalidation/finalization, no live fallback was fetched, and current locked withdrawals are about 1.25% of verified pooled ETH while accounting performance covers about 100%.

evidence.shows: Oracle members 3, quorum 2, reportPeriodSlot 1280, paused false.
Admin references Oracle/LP/RoleRegistry; rebase APR 500; wait 50 slots.
Admin source: executeTasks checks oracle consensus; withdrawals can be invalidated/finalized; APR/fee checks bounded.
LP pooled ETH 1892812811272698485017379; locked withdrawal ETH 23740121436340809603728; ratio about 1.25%.
PriorityQueue source: fulfill onlyRequestManager; invalidate can target pending/finalized.
Fetched body says weETH cross-chain bridges/mints via LayerZero.

unknowns: A2: Oracle identities/bonding/selection not fetched.
A2: Node-operator set/diversification/bonding not verified.
A3: Cross-chain TVL and bridge model not quantified.
A6: No fallback/challenge for withdrawal invalidation found.
A9: Exit window for dependency changes not reconstructed.

headline: Core staking and standard withdrawal contracts admit users directly on-chain without a whitelist; official UI region-blocking and a whitelisted priority queue are context.

findings.text: LP whitelist disabled; normal deposit/standard withdraw-request not allowlist-gated. PriorityQueue request placement onlyWhitelisted.
Normal LP deposits/standard withdraw requests require no operator admission approval.
Official UI region-blocks and terms restrict some jurisdictions.
Independent access exists through verified ABIs/source, public repo and direct calls.
No on-chain sanctions/blocklist found in fetched LP/eETH/WRNFT/PriorityQueue surfaces.
Reads public; core deposit/standard request writes public subject to pause; priority/privileged functions gated.
Terms restrict Canada/restricted jurisdictions; blocked page says platform unavailable in region.

steelman.red: Priority withdrawals are whitelisted and official UI region-blocks users.
steelman.orange: Operational capture would apply if no independent path existed.
steelman.green: Core deposit and standard withdraw requests are not contract-whitelisted and are directly callable.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because core staking and standard exit admission is contract-permissionless and directly callable; priority whitelist and UI/ToS restrictions do not gate the normal path.

evidence.shows: LP whitelist false, paused false, requestWithdraw exposed.
PriorityQueue source: request onlyWhitelisted; claims not onlyWhitelisted.
Official blocked page says access restricted/unavailable.
Terms modified 2026-04-03 restrict jurisdictions and distinguish Stake/Liquid.

unknowns: A3b: No third-party frontend/wallet integration fetched.
A4: Full peripheral blocklist grep not completed.
